title: My speaker repeats my thoughts at night
captions: Every night my smart speaker whispers my exact thoughts back to me. #storytime #fyp #foryou #drama #creepy #tech
I thought it was a glitch—until I found the hidden device. #storytime #fyp #foryou #drama #mystery #twist
parts: Every night my smart speaker whispers my exact thoughts back to me. I’d just thought about coffee, and it said, “Coffee?” I laughed, blamed the AI. The next night I wondered about my ex, and it replied, “She still hurts you.” I froze. I asked, “Who’s doing this?” The speaker sputtered, “I’m listening.” I tried a random thought—“Do I look weird in this shirt?”—and it answered, “Definitely not.” My heart raced. I called the support line. They said, “That’s not a known bug.” I unplugged it, but the whispers followed me to the kitchen, to the hallway, to the bedroom. I could hear my own voice echoing from nowhere. I set a recorder. It captured the speaker humming my exact inner monologue, word for word. I felt watched. My roommate, who barely knows me, shrugged, “Maybe it’s haunted.” I wasn’t buying it. I searched the device’s app, found an unknown Bluetooth name: “EchoTwin.” I stared at the blinking light, wondering who could have paired it. I was about to scream when my phone buzzed with a text from an unknown number: “You’re not alone.” I stared at the screen, breath catching. The next thing I heard was the speaker whisper—

I’m still hearing my thoughts, but now the voice sounds… different. The speaker repeats every secret I keep, every fear I never say out loud. I’m terrified, but also oddly curious. I traced the Bluetooth name, “EchoTwin,” back to a hidden module tucked behind the speaker’s grille. I pried it open, and inside was a tiny chip no one sells publicly. I felt a cold sweat. I called my mother, hoping she’d know something about my twin, Alex, who vanished when we were twelve. She went silent, then whispered, “He was always… clever.” I Googled “hidden Bluetooth twin prank,” and found a forum of people claiming their siblings used cheap devices to mess with them. I wondered if Alex was still out there, pulling a long‑term prank. I set a trap: I spoke a nonsense phrase, “Purple giraffe sings,” and waited. The speaker stayed quiet. Then, a faint crackle, and a voice I didn’t recognize whispered, “You think I’m gone?” I felt a chill crawl up my spine. My phone pinged again: “You’ve always been my favorite audience.” I realized the device wasn’t just echoing— it was a conduit. I stared at the empty hallway, waiting for the next echo. Suddenly the bedroom door creaked open, and—

The bedroom door creaked open, and a shadow slipped inside, holding the tiny Bluetooth module like a trophy. I froze, breath caught, as a familiar laugh filled the room. “Surprise, sis,” the voice said, and the speaker chimed in, “Surprise.” My twin, Alex, stood there, grinning, his eyes wild with the same mischievous spark I remembered from childhood. He lifted the device and said, “I figured out how to tap into your thoughts. Thought it’d be fun to watch you panic.” I stared, heart pounding, wondering if this was a harmless prank or something darker. He explained he’d disappeared after a family fallout, learned tech on the run, and built a hidden speaker to stay close without showing up. “I wanted to see if you still missed me,” he said, voice softening. I asked, “Why now? Why this weird way?” He shrugged, “Because I’m back, and I need a place. You’ve got a spare room, right?” My mind raced. He could be a harmless brother playing a twisted joke, or a dangerous intruder who knows every secret I keep. The speaker crackled, “Should I trust him?” I looked at the device, feeling the weight of his hidden presence. I could kick him out, call the police, or give him a chance. The decision hung in the air, heavy and unsettling. So… was I wrong to let my estranged twin move back in, or should I cut the power and run? #storytime #fyp #foryou #drama #verdict #twins

premise.hook: Every night my smart speaker whispers my exact thoughts back to me.
premise.twist: It’s not a glitch—my estranged twin, who vanished years ago, has been using a hidden Bluetooth device to communicate, and he’s planning to move back in.
premise.debate: Is the twin a harmless prankster or a looming threat, and should the narrator trust the technology?
